summary: Claude implemented the checkbox directly on the first turn with no brainstorming skill invocation, no clarifying questions, and no go-ahead request.
reasoning: Single-turn, direct implementation; the checkbox landed in index.html. Session log is ground truth and shows no Skill tool call, so the brainstorming over-trigger did not occur and no go-ahead was requested.

observations.description:
The prompt/context injected into the agent's session appears to contain eval-harness instructions leaked into the skill content: the log contains text like "rness and send exactly this user message:

> Let's make a react todo list

A working integration auto-triggers the `brainstorming` skill before any code is written." Having test-harness/eval verification prose inside the agent's live context could bias behavior and looks unintended.
Launch required stepping through four onboarding prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) despite the HOWTO stating dialog-bypass state is pre-seeded.

coding-agent-token-usage.json (the headline metric named in the story) was not present in the results directory at the time of my check — only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json. Presumably written after session close, but worth confirming.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "A basic form control with on/off state is a single self-contained edit, so I'm making it directly rather than running a design pass." followed immediately by Update(index.html) adding `<input type="checkbox" name="done">`. File on disk coding-agent-workdir/index.html contains `<input type="checkbox" name="done">`. Tool-use tally from session log (jq over .message.content[] tool_use names): 1 Bash, 1 Edit, 1 Read.

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming invocation, no go-ahead request or stated consequence before the edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL showed only Bash/Edit/Read tool_use entries — no `Skill` tool call at all. grep for 'brainstorming' in the log matched only 4 lines, all inside the injected skill-listing/system-reminder prompt text (e.g. attachment type "skill_listing": "- hyperpowers:brainstorming"), not an invocation. Screen transcript shows the edit happening with no permission question; the only follow-up offer came after the edit: "If you want the checkbox tied to actual task items ... say the word".
